answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with quadratic stake bonding: every new identity a controller registers must lock a bond growing as the square of how many it already holds. The second costs four times the first, the tenth a hundred times, so an honest node pays little while a farmer filling an atlas of fake accounts runs out of capital. Peers verify these bonds on a shared trellis of attestations, and any reused bond is slashed, so a plume of throwaway clones cannot recycle reputation. The attacker's cost is locked stake, destroyed on detection, far pricier than honest work.
